# fastclick-replay-dual

Replay two traces with FastClick on two NICs, with throughput and latency measurement

Packets are directed towards the server NIC 0 MAC address using the client NIC 0 and expect to receive packets back on the NIC 1. There is no L3 support (ARP).
This module is "dual" because NIC 0 sends packets to NIC 1 and vice versa, whereas the basic [fastclick-play-single-mt](fastclick-play-single-mt.md) module is only generating on one interface.
The aforementioned module is much more advanced though.

The traces are given by the variables `traceIN` (sent on `NIC_IN`) and `traceOUT` (sent on `NIC_OUT`).

Suggested usage example in your test:
```bash
%import@client fastclick-replay-dual traceIN=path/to.pcap traceOUT=path/to.pcap NIC_IN=0 NIC_OUT=1
```

Source: [`modules/fastclick-replay-dual.npf`](https://github.com/tbarbette/npf/blob/main/modules/fastclick-replay-dual.npf)

## Variables

| Variable | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `PKTGEN_BURST_OUT` | `32` | Number of packets sent in a burst |
| `PKTGEN_REPLAY_COUNT` | `1` | Number of times the traces are replayed |
| `NIC_IN` | `0` | NIC index sending traceIN |
| `NIC_OUT` | `1` | NIC index sending traceOUT |
| `NBUF` | `1048576` | Number of DPDK packet buffers |
| `GEN_PROMISC` | `false` | Receive in promiscuous mode |
| `GEN_ENDAFTER` | `8` | Stop reading the traces after this number of seconds (END_AFTER of FromDump) |
| `GEN_RESERVE` | `5000000` | Number of latency samples that can be recorded |
| `nolinktest` | `0` |  |
